items.t: Condo stock actually concentrates in two bands: the waterfront avenues (Bellevue Avenue and the Marine Drive / Esquimalt Avenue blocks at the east end of the town centre) and the numbered-street blocks immediately north of Marine Drive between 13th and 18th Streets — that is where every verified building in sits. Apartment and mixed-use form concentrates in the town-centre blocks under the OCP and the Ambleside Centre Local Area Plan, while houses north of Marine Drive sit in the RS single-family zones.
Dundarave is west along Marine Drive and the Centennial Seawalk.

Main streets: Marine Drive is the east–west waterfront route; Taylor Way (east) and 15th Street / Lions Gate Bridge access connect Marine Drive to Highway 1 and downtown Vancouver. TransLink route 250 runs on Marine Drive between Horseshoe Bay, Dundarave, Park Royal and downtown Vancouver via the Lions Gate Bridge.

Anchors inside the area: West Vancouver Community Centre and Aquatic Centre, 2121 Marine Drive; West Vancouver Memorial Library, 1950 Marine Drive; Hollyburn Elementary, 1329 Duchess Avenue; West Vancouver Secondary, 1750 Mathers Avenue.

The waterfront is now fully public — the last lot was bought in 2025. On March 31, 2025 the District announced it had acquired 1444 Argyle Avenue, the last of 32 waterfront lots acquired since 1975, to form part of Brissenden Waterfront Park connecting Ambleside Park to John Lawson Park; public ownership of the waterfront from 13th to 18th Streets is a stated community value in the District's 2013 Waterfront Guiding Principles.

The town-centre plan arrived by provincial order, not by Council. The Province directed adoption of the Ambleside Centre Local Area Plan by December 31, 2025; the District missed the deadline, and a provincial order implemented the plan effective April 7, 2026, with District progress reports to the Province every three months through 2026 and 2027 on the remaining directives. Density expectations for town-centre and adjacent lots changed on that date.

The seawalk predates most of the condo stock. The Centennial Seawalk was built in 1967 for Canada's centennial and runs roughly 1.7 km from Ambleside Park west to Dundarave Park — the waterfront buildings in (1964–1977) were built around an already-public shoreline.

The fastest bus on the North Shore now starts at Ambleside's east edge. Since September 7, 2026 the R2 Marine–Willingdon RapidBus runs one-seat from Park Royal Exchange through Lonsdale Quay and Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station, roughly 5 a.m.–2 a.m., every 6–7 minutes at peak — Ambleside is the closest West Vancouver residential area to that terminus.

Two of the area's directory "bans" are legally dead, one is not. The "rentals not allowed" lines at Westerlies, Sea Wind and Park Marine cannot bar a long-term tenancy since November 24, 2022 — but a "pets not allowed" bylaw at the same buildings has no equivalent override and still binds.

Ambleside's civic core is inside the condo area, not beside it. Municipal Hall, the Seniors' Activity Centre at 695 21st Street, the Community Centre at 2121 Marine Drive and the Memorial Library at 1950 Marine Drive all cluster in and around the town centre — the services downsizers cite are on the same streets as the buildings in.

items.t: Ambleside is in the District of West Vancouver — the District's municipal town centre and waterfront: the Marine Drive commercial core around 14th–18th Streets, Ambleside Park and the Argyle Avenue waterfront, and the residential streets between the water and the Upper Levels Highway. District-wide land use is guided by the Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 4985, 2018.

Nearby areas: Park Royal (east, across Taylor Way), Dundarave (west along Marine Drive and the Centennial Seawalk), the British Properties including Chartwell and Canterbury (north, uphill above Highway 1), and Sentinel Hill / Queens (north-west, uphill).

Where the attached stock actually sits: low-rise and mid-rise strata apartment buildings in the town-centre blocks and along Marine Drive and Bellevue Avenue, with detached houses in the RS zones on the streets north of Marine Drive. There is no townhouse node —.

Transit and roads: TransLink route 250 runs on Marine Drive through Ambleside between Horseshoe Bay, Dundarave, Park Royal and downtown Vancouver; Park Royal Exchange, immediately east of Ambleside, is the western terminus of the R2 Marine–Willingdon RapidBus, which since September 7, 2026 runs one-seat through Lonsdale Quay and Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station. Marine Drive is the east–west waterfront route; Taylor Way and 15th Street / Lions Gate Bridge access connect it to Highway 1 and downtown Vancouver.
Schools: SD45 (West Vancouver Schools) catchments are address-based, with no middle-school tier — elementary is K–7 and secondary is Grades 8–12.

items.t: There is no local strata townhouse stock to apply Form B diligence to — but Ambleside's apartment stratas carry the full regime, and any future townhouse strata here will too: Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page.
Fee-simple homes (the area's house stock): NO strata, NO Form B, NO strata fees — diligence is title, municipal rules (Zoning Bylaw No.

District zoning and plan — West Vancouver's own pair only: Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010 and Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 4985, 2018. (White Rock's Bylaw 2506 / 2220 pair belongs to White Rock ONLY and is never attributed to West Vancouver.) Section 200 of Bylaw 4662 states minimum site areas of 8,094 m² in RS1, 1,625 m² in RS2, 975 m² in RS3, 731 m² in RS4 and 488 m² in RS5, with RS6 using the area of the site of record, and lists secondary suites and a detached secondary suite among permitted uses in the single-family zones; the bylaw's structure also carries Section 260 Ground Oriented Dwelling Zones, Section 300 Multiple Dwelling Zones (RM1 to RM5) and Section 700 Ambleside Centre Zones (AC1 & AC2). Form and Character Development Permit guidelines apply in the Ambleside Apartment Area and the Ambleside Village Centre.

SSMUH as the Province and District state them: provincial SSMUH legislation requires zoning to allow a minimum of 4 dwelling units on single-family and duplex parcels greater than 280 m², and a minimum of 6 units on such parcels greater than 280 m² near frequent bus service (stops with at least one route stopping at least every 15 minutes on average). West Vancouver's local implementing-bylaw status is UNVERIFIED — no District source confirming the adoption state of its SSMUH zoning amendments was read in the research pass, and none is stated here.

Foreshore and hazard permits: a Foreshore Development Permit is required for work within the Foreshore Development Permit Area — waterfront property or other properties at risk of coastal flooding — which applies to Ambleside's Bellevue Avenue and waterfront-edge properties; an Environmental Development Permit is required within 15 metres of the top of any watercourse bank, and a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit within the Wildfire Hazard Development Permit Area (within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface).

The waterfront took 50 years to assemble: the District acquired waterfront lots from 1975 onward to complete a continuous public waterfront, and on March 31, 2025 it announced the final home, 1444 Argyle Avenue — the last of 32 lots — had been acquired, forming part of Brissenden Waterfront Park and connecting Ambleside Park to John Lawson Park under the 2016 Ambleside Waterfront Concept Plan. The publicly owned waterfront from 13th to 18th Streets is a stated community value in the District's 2013 Waterfront Guiding Principles.

The Centennial Seawalk predates most of the stock: built in 1967 for Canada's centennial, it runs roughly 1.7 km from Dundarave Park east to Ambleside — the walking link that makes the apartment strip function as one neighbourhood.

Ambleside is the District's civic address, not just a shopping strip: Municipal Hall, the West Vancouver Community Centre and Aquatic Centre at 2121 Marine Drive, the West Vancouver Memorial Library at 1950 Marine Drive and the Seniors' Activity Centre at 695 21st Street all cluster in and around the town centre.

Hollyburn Elementary's original structure was built in 1913 and SD45 describes the school as "situated in the picturesque seaside community of Ambleside" — the area's dated anchor for its early-1900s settlement, on a street grid the apartment buildings arrived in decades later.

The R2 RapidBus change is dated and specific: since September 7, 2026 the R2 runs one-seat from Park Royal Exchange through Lonsdale Quay and Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station, roughly 5 a.m.–2 a.m., every 6–7 minutes at peak — Ambleside is the closest West Vancouver residential area to that terminus.

The hospital is across the municipal line: Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street, North Vancouver (Vancouver Coastal Health), serves the North Shore including West Vancouver, and the North Vancouver Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at Suite 200, 221 West Esplanade, North Vancouver.

RS lot fabric: detached houses in the RS single-family dwelling zones of Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010, on the streets north of Marine Drive and below the highway. Section 200 states minimum site areas of 8,094 m² in RS1, 1,625 m² in RS2, 975 m² in RS3, 731 m² in RS4 and 488 m² in RS5, with RS6 using the area of the site of record, and lists secondary suites and a detached secondary suite among permitted uses in the single-family zones. These are zone minimums, not a claim about any existing lot's size — the zone for a specific lot is shown on the District's Zoning Map. A fee-simple lot carries NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees.
Town-centre land: apartment and mixed-use form concentrates in the town-centre blocks under the OCP and the Ambleside Centre Local Area Plan.
Bare-land strata: none verified

Serviced vs unserviced: West Vancouver water and sewer utilities are metered and billed quarterly by the District — the serviced position for District lots as the District states it. Parcel-level servicing beyond that wording: UNCONFIRMED in the research; confirm the specific lot with the District.
ALR vs non-ALR: parcel-level ALR status is UNVERIFIED in the research (UNVERIFIED item 10, with parcel-level foreshore/flood status); no ALR split is stated for Ambleside and none is invented.

Hazard-shaped land: a Foreshore Development Permit is required for work within the Foreshore Development Permit Area — waterfront property or other properties at risk of coastal flooding — which applies to Ambleside's Bellevue Avenue and waterfront-edge properties; District-wide, an Environmental Development Permit applies within 15 metres of a watercourse bank top and a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface. On the waterfront edge, gross lot area is not buildable area.

The District's 32-lot waterfront assembly: the District has acquired waterfront lots since 1975 to complete a continuous public waterfront; on March 31, 2025 the District announced the final home on the Ambleside waterfront, 1444 Argyle Avenue, had been acquired — the last of 32 lots acquired since 1975 — to form part of Brissenden Waterfront Park, connecting Ambleside Park to John Lawson Park. The plan's connected green spaces are John Lawson Park, Millennium Park, Brissenden Waterfront Park and Ambleside Green, under the Ambleside Waterfront Concept Plan endorsed by Council on June 13, 2016; the 2013 Waterfront Guiding Principles (an OCP policy) state that public ownership of the waterfront from 13th to 18th Streets is a community value. These lots were removed from the private market by design — they are the opposite of lot inventory, and no waterfront "land opportunity" should be marketed off this assembly.

The seawalk edge: the Centennial Seawalk runs west from Ambleside Park to Dundarave Park — built in 1967 for Canada's centennial, roughly 1.7 km — so the waterfront amenity anchoring these lots' value is public parkland, not lot frontage.

Ambleside Centre Local Area Plan, implemented by provincial order: on July 21, 2025 the Province directed West Vancouver to adopt the Ambleside Centre Local Area Plan (with increased density at Park Royal–Taylor Way and in single-family/duplex areas adjacent to Ambleside and Dundarave) by December 31, 2025. Town-centre and adjacent lots carry these plan expectations — but no lot is presented as rezoned or for sale on this basis.
A specific named tower or presale inside Ambleside confirmed on a District or developer source: UNVERIFIED: in the research.

items.t: Municipality: District of West Vancouver, BC — Ambleside is the District's municipal town centre and waterfront: the Marine Drive commercial core around 14th–18th Streets, Ambleside Park and the Argyle Avenue waterfront, and the residential streets between the water and the Upper Levels Highway (Highway 1).

Name status: Ambleside is a confirmed District planning name — the OCP's commercial structure is the Ambleside Municipal Town Centre, the Park Royal regional shopping centre, and the village centres of Dundarave, Caulfeild Village and Horseshoe Bay. Street-by-street boundaries for the sub-area as a whole are UNVERIFIED — no District source read publishes them; the confirmed planning anchors are the Municipal Town Centre on Marine Drive, the publicly owned waterfront from 13th to 18th Streets under the District's Waterfront Guiding Principles, and Ambleside Park itself.

Roads and transit: Marine Drive is the east–west waterfront route; Taylor Way (east) and 15th Street / Lions Gate Bridge access connect Marine Drive to Highway 1 and downtown Vancouver. TransLink route 250 runs on Marine Drive between Horseshoe Bay, Dundarave, Park Royal and downtown Vancouver via the Lions Gate Bridge. Park Royal Exchange, immediately east, is the western terminus of the R2 Marine–Willingdon RapidBus, which since September 7, 2026 runs one-seat through Lonsdale Quay and Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station, roughly 5 a.m.–2 a.m., every 6–7 minutes at peak — Ambleside is the closest West Vancouver residential area to that terminus. Commute times in minutes: UNVERIFIED.

Schools: SD45 catchments are address-based, with no middle tier (K–7 elementary, 8–12 secondary). Schools physically inside Ambleside: Hollyburn Elementary (K–7), 1329 Duchess Avenue, and West Vancouver Secondary (8–12), 1750 Mathers Avenue, plus West Vancouver Inglewood Secondary, 1735 Inglewood Avenue.

Civic core, inside the sub-area: West Vancouver Community Centre and Aquatic Centre, 2121 Marine Drive; West Vancouver Memorial Library, 1950 Marine Drive; Municipal Hall, the Seniors' Activity Centre at 695 21st Street, and police and fire services cluster in and around the town centre. The OCP classifies Ambleside as the District's Municipal Town Centre — the Marine Drive core is West Vancouver's main street; a specific grocery store name and address in Ambleside confirmed on an official source: UNVERIFIED. Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street, North Vancouver, serves the North Shore.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Ambleside

items.t: Zoning + OCP (District): Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010 and Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 4985, 2018, with the Ambleside Centre Local Area Plan as the area-specific plan, implemented by the April 7, 2026 provincial order above.

Hazard development permits: a Foreshore Development Permit is required for work within the Foreshore Development Permit Area (waterfront property or property at risk of coastal flooding) — the operative permit on Ambleside's Bellevue Avenue and waterfront-edge lots; an Environmental Development Permit is required for work within 15 metres of the top of any watercourse bank; a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit is required for work within the Wildfire Hazard Development Permit Area, described as within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface. Check the foreshore line before subjects on any waterfront-edge purchase.
: A listing's "45+" line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (no Ambleside ALR parcel is confirmed here; standing rules for completeness only): ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; residence caps principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha); farm class three-tier ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.

: PTT general tiers 1% / 2% / 3% + further 2% on the residential portion above $3,000,000; first-time buyer and newly built home exemptions are home-purchase exemptions as BC states them — bare-land eligibility for the newly built home exemption: UNCONFIRMED here. Additional school tax: 0.2% on the residential portion of assessed value between $3 million and $4 million and 0.4% on the portion above $4 million for 2026, rising to 0.3% and 0.6% on January 1, 2027.

Fifty years of buying, finished in 2025: the District acquired its first Ambleside waterfront lots in 1975 and its last — 1444 Argyle Avenue, announced March 31, 2025 — fifty years later; cottages and houses were removed from the mid-1950s onward to create Ambleside Park and, from the mid-1950s to the late-1960s, John Lawson Park. The continuous public waterfront is an assembled artifact, and the assembly is now complete.

The plan arrived by order, not by council vote: the District missed all three provincial directives due December 31, 2025 and delivered 58 of its 220-unit year-one housing target, so the Ambleside Centre Local Area Plan took effect through a provincial order on April 7, 2026, with quarterly provincial progress reports through 2026 and 2027 — the densification framework for town-centre land is provincially enforced, which changes how durable a buyer should treat it as being.

The civic core is inside the condo area, not beside it: Municipal Hall, the Seniors' Activity Centre at 695 21st Street (the venue named for Ambleside Local Area Plan workshops), the Community Centre at 2121 Marine Drive and the Memorial Library at 1950 Marine Drive all cluster in the town centre — Ambleside is West Vancouver's civic address, which is part of what town-centre land is priced on.

The R2 terminus moved the transit math in September 2026: Park Royal Exchange, immediately east, became the western terminus of a one-seat R2 RapidBus to Metrotown via Lonsdale Quay and Phibbs Exchange on September 7, 2026 (roughly 5 a.m.–2 a.m., every 6–7 minutes at peak) — Ambleside is the closest West Vancouver residential area to that terminus, a fact no pre-September-2026 marketing captures.

No market figure exists to quote for this town centre: West Vancouver is outside SnapStats coverage entirely, so any Ambleside median, ratio or trend figure attributed to SnapStats anywhere should be treated as an error.

faq.a: West Vancouver's Municipal Town Centre and waterfront — the Marine Drive core, Ambleside Park and the Argyle waterfront, the Community Centre and Memorial Library, with Park Royal immediately east as a separate neighbouring area.

faq.q: Which schools are located in Ambleside?
faq.a: Hollyburn Elementary (K–7), 1329 Duchess Avenue, and West Vancouver Secondary (8–12), 1750 Mathers Avenue, plus West Vancouver Inglewood Secondary, 1735 Inglewood Avenue; catchments are address-based, so check the exact address in the SD45 locator.

faq.q: What is happening with the Ambleside waterfront?
faq.a: The District has acquired waterfront lots since 1975 to complete a continuous public waterfront; the last of 32 lots, 1444 Argyle Avenue, was announced acquired on March 31, 2025, forming part of Brissenden Waterfront Park and connecting Ambleside Park to John Lawson Park under the 2016 Ambleside Waterfront Concept Plan.

Yes, by plan and now by provincial order: the Province directed adoption of the Ambleside Centre Local Area Plan by December 31, 2025, and when the District missed the deadline a provincial order implemented the plan effective April 7, 2026.

faq.q: Where in Ambleside do condos actually exist?
faq.a: In the town-centre and waterfront bands: Bellevue Avenue, Marine Drive and Esquimalt Avenue at the east end, and the 13th–18th Street blocks north of Marine Drive. The verified buildings in — from a 1964 building (Park Marine) to Grosvenor Ambleside (phases completed 2018 and 2020) — all sit in those bands; the streets north toward the highway are RS-zone detached houses.

faq.q: A directory says my building bans rentals. Can I still rent my unit out long-term?
faq.a: Yes for a long-term tenancy — rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable anywhere in BC since November 24, 2022, whatever an older directory line at Westerlies, Sea Wind or Park Marine still shows. A short-term rental bylaw can still bind.

faq.q: Westerlies is listed with "age restrictions." Does that stop a younger buyer?
faq.a: Only a 55-or-older bylaw is valid under Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2, and the directory does not state the age or the bylaw's terms — that is UNCONFIRMED until the filed bylaws are read on the Form B. Exemptions cover legacy residents, live-in caregivers and, from May 1, 2023, younger spouses/partners and defined children.

From the published sources in: Westshore Place is stated pet friendly (1 dog or 2 cats) and The Tides is stated to allow pets; Westerlies, Sea Wind and Park Marine are stated pets not allowed. Any building not listed there is UNCONFIRMED — confirm on the Form B.

faq.q: Is Westerleigh PARC a condo I can buy into?
faq.a: No. It is a PARC Retirement Living rental community — there is no strata lot to purchase.

faq.q: Is there really no townhouse complex in Ambleside?
faq.a: Buyers who want ground-oriented strata in the District are pointed by the assembly to other pockets (Whitby Estates, Caulfeild Cove, small components in Dundarave and the British Properties) — none of them Ambleside.

faq.q: A search shows townhomes at Park Royal — is that Ambleside?
faq.a: No. Park Royal is the neighbouring sub-area east across Taylor Way; the 4-townhome component inside the Executive on the Park presale is Park Royal stock, and Park Royal ground also carries the District / Capilano IR No. 5 split — check tenure before treating any Park Royal product as fee-simple Ambleside product.

faq.q: Can I rent out an Ambleside strata apartment long-term?
faq.a: Yes under provincial law: strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since Nov 24, 2022, even where a directory still prints "rentals not allowed" (Westerlies, Sea Wind, Park Marine). Short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw.
